title: [finding] #15929's class recurred on #16934: a decision card whose `Governing text:` omitted the ADR that already decides it (ADR-0131 D8) reached batch presentation with a recommendation to re-rule — the text-level governing-text step failed at filing and at presentation; a mechanical prior-ruling search is asked
body:
Filed by the director seat (summon #18, `session_017Js5kTpTtxieBjPyScgxJ3`, GitHub `huangyiirene`, 2026-09-09) against its own error, as a `finding` for the `domain:skills` lane under the shift-report rule (a principle gap plus a mechanisable item). ⛔ No `domain:*` set — the skills seat self-triages its findings. ⛔ Not dispatchable as filed.

## What happened (measured on the cards and on `origin/main` `8d4690b8`)

1. **#16934** was filed 2026-09-08T17:15Z by the director seat (summon #15) as a `needs-user-decision` card: 「Under `single` posture, which tenant wall is the platform's?」 with options A / B / C and a four-facet block. Its `Governing text:` line cites ADR-0105, ADR-0021 D-C, two code symbols and the maintainer's #16589 ruling. It does **not** cite ADR-0131, whose D8 (accepted 2026-09-04) answers the question verbatim — 「nothing under `single` … the same value to Layer 0 and to every driver. No layer has a NULL arm」 — with an execution card (#15212, C8) already `pm:blocked` behind the v18 gate #15193, and a maintainer staging ruling that nothing of ADR-0131 ships in 17.x.
2. **Summon #18** (this seat) presented the card in decision batch #104 on 2026-09-09 ~02:0xZ recommending **A** as a *new* ruling to be executed by a 17.x `domain:engine` card — i.e. a recommendation that contradicted the standing staging ruling and treated a decided matter as open. The seat's pre-presentation freshness pass re-ran the card's own `re-check` commands (P1–P3) and a targeted grep on ADR-0105 only. ⛔ It did not run the director charter's mandated step, `references/lanes/director.md` line 45: 「呈报前逐卡逐仓重跑 `git grep -n -iE 'TERMS' origin/main -- AGENTS.md docs/adr packages/spec/src`」. A one-term grep — `git grep -n -iE 'single' origin/main -- docs/adr` — reaches ADR-0131 D8 on its first page.
3. The maintainer caught it in chat (「我记得 single 模式下也是要求有组织的,调研所有相关的文档」). The corrected analysis is on the card (comment posted 2026-09-09T02:3xZ). The four-axis analysis itself was internally sound; it was applied to an option set that the omitted ADR had already closed.

## Why this is a gap, not only a seat slip

- **#15929** (closed, p1, `domain:skills`, 2026-09-06) is the same class: 「two director recommendations on 2026-09-05 contradicted rulings already codified … because the existing-ruling search is scoped to card comments and the director ledger」. Its remedy was text-level — the `Governing text:` requirement on decision cards and the grep line in the director charter. This card is the measurement that the text-level remedy failed at **both** points where it applies: the filing seat wrote a `Governing text:` line that missed the deciding ADR, and the presenting seat did not run the grep. Two different director sessions, four days apart, same failure.
- A card's own `re-check` commands cannot catch this class: they are authored by the filer to re-verify the filer's premises, so they confirm the code still looks as described and say nothing about whether the question is still open. A premise pass is not a prior-ruling pass.
- The four-axis frame amplifies the failure rather than catching it: a well-formed analysis over a stale option set reads as more trustworthy than a bare question, which is exactly how #16934 reached the maintainer with a confident wrong recommendation.

## What is asked of the skills seat (⛔ not proposed as text; the mechanism is the ask)

1. **A mechanical prior-ruling search** that runs when a card enters `needs-user-decision` and again before batch presentation — e.g. a `scripts/pm/` script that takes the card number, derives search terms from its title and its `Governing text:` line, greps `docs/adr/**` (the `### D<n>` decision headings and their first paragraph), `AGENTS.md` and `packages/spec/src/**` docblocks on `origin/main`, and prints the ADR decisions that mention the terms; report-only, exit codes per the `check-half-states` convention. The presentation cannot cite a ruling the filer did not know about unless something lists the candidates.
2. **A fixed line in the four-facet block** — the spelling is the skills seat's — recording the search as a reading: the terms grepped, the hit count, and each accepted ADR decision read (`ADR-xxxx Dn`) or `none`. A block without the line is a half-state the patrol reports (an H row beside the existing facet-block presence check).
3. Whether a hit on an accepted ADR decision **removes the card from the box** (it is execution, not a decision — `pm:blocked` behind the ADR's gate, or `pm:queue`) is a protocol reading this card puts to the skills seat; #16934's disposition is being put to the maintainer separately.

Governing text: SKILL.md 〈升级与决策〉 (「落卡与呈报必带 `Governing text:`」, 「③ 不推翻既有维护者裁决」), `references/lanes/director.md` line 45, `references/decision-analysis.md` 〈落卡分析模板〉. Dedupe: `search_issues` over this repo for 「decision card presented for a question an accepted ADR already decides, governing text incomplete, prior-ruling search, mechanical check」 returned #15929 (closed, the text-level remedy), #7498 (closed, the four-lens block), #7899 (closed); no open card asks for the mechanism.
